public_summary: Iran remains in sustained stealth blackout posture: all four major ISP international gateways are externally unreachable while BGP routes hold and domestic services function normally. The gateway failure-mode taxonomy has stabilized into two patterns — active TCP RST (TIC GW 1, Irancell) and silent drop (TIC GW 2, Asiatech) — indicating mature, per-node DPI configuration. A notable improvement: Saman Bank latency dropped to 2,963ms from 4,260ms, suggesting NIN congestion relief. The protocol whitelist continues to allow only ~4.2% of IP ranges (45/1068) to respond externally.
insight: The stabilization of gateway failure modes into two clean categories (active RST vs. silent drop) across multiple observation passes suggests Iran's filtering infrastructure has reached operational maturity — the earlier behavioral shifts (e.g., Irancell transitioning from timeout to connection refused) were one-time configuration tuning, not ongoing instability; the system is now in a steady-state stealth filtering posture with predictable per-node behavior.
recommendation: Monitor Saman Bank latency as a leading indicator of NIN congestion dynamics — the drop from 4,260ms to 2,963ms breaks the upward oscillation trend (3197→3615→3340→4260→2963ms), but whether this signals genuine capacity improvement or a temporary lull before the next spike requires continued tracking. Also worth correlating NIN traffic patterns with time-of-day to distinguish peak-hour congestion from sustained infrastructure pressure.
